prize_parts.citation: For the rational design of molecular-sieve catalysts, using structure-directing synthesis to create new pore architectures and place active sites within them

statement.case_for: After the first round I still hold B013, but with a narrower claim than before. The achievement is the deliberate use of organic structure-directing agents and synthesis design to obtain new zeolite frameworks and to place catalytic sites inside defined pores, so that shape selectivity and acidity can be engineered rather than found. Zones (SSZ-type materials and structure-directing agents at Chevron), Davis (synthesis concepts, new framework types, site-isolated catalysts) and Corma (catalyst design for acid, redox and bifunctional sites, deployed at scale) each supply a distinct, independently confirmed part of that story. Structures are solved crystallographically, and increasingly by 3D electron diffraction for nanocrystalline products, so the structure-to-function link is verified rather than asserted. The field is decades mature, widely deployed in refining and emission control, and solidly chemistry. No other first choice on the table combines maturity, confirmed structure and clear chemical content to the same degree.
statement.case_against: The citation is still broader than I would like, and the three-name cap forces a cut that excludes Yu and Tsapatsis and ignores the earlier work of Barrer, Breck and Flanigen. No colleague has moved toward B013 in round 1, and I remain its only supporter, so the committee should treat my vote with the discount that a specialist preference deserves, particularly since this is my own field and I cannot be fully detached. The chair's questions also show that B007 and B061 hold the most support and that I have not given a persuasive reason why the committee should converge on a ballot nobody else ranks first. I do not claim that it is more important than degraders or base editing, only that it is more mature and more clearly settled in credit and mechanism.

responses.point: Chabes puts B007 first with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, arguing that cereblon explains the molecular-glue branch and unifies it with heterobifunctional degraders.
responses.response: I take the cereblon argument seriously: the identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target and the ternary-complex structures are exactly the kind of verified structural evidence I weigh most. But it shows the difficulty for the chair's question. A PROTAC is a rational design (Crews, Deshaies), whereas cereblon is a target identification that explains drugs found empirically. Putting them under one citation risks two stories sharing one sentence, and Ciulli, Sakamoto, Ito and Gray each have a claim equal to Handa's. If the committee settles on B007 I would prefer the narrower concept citation and Crews and Deshaies, with Handa only if the citation is written around the mechanism. I still cannot call the field mature without an approved degrader, so I keep it as my first alternative rather than my first choice.

responses.point: Aili proposes Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, with a PROTAC-centred citation on induced-proximity design and the glue strand kept separate.
responses.response: Of the three B007 configurations this is the one I find most coherent, because Ciulli's VHL ligands and the structural work on cooperativity are what made ternary complexes a design variable, and I can judge that evidence on structural grounds. I agree with Daniel that separating PROTACs from glues keeps the citation honest. I disagree on timing. Late-stage trials are not approval, and he lists the absence of an approved degrader himself as a risk. A prize built on a designed modality should be able to point to a drug that works in patients, and for zeolite catalysts the equivalent proof has existed for decades. If an approval arrives I would move to this configuration.

responses.point: Brzezinski proposes two parts, Crews and Deshaies for degraders and Liu for base editing, as one achievement on proteins and one on nucleic acids, with no double count.
responses.response: The pairing is transparent about what it does, but I do not see a shared principle beyond acting on two kinds of biomolecule, and the cap of three names forces it to drop Ciulli and Handa to fit. I would accept it as a reasonable majority route, and as the committee's most supported pairing it deserves a serious hearing. My objection is the same as for a single part: it combines the two entries whose maturity is most disputed (no approved degrader, base editing a decade old and following the 2020 prize). A two-part prize stacked on two open timing questions seems to me less secure than one settled part.

responses.point: Aqvist argues for Liu alone on base editing as a simple chemical idea with clean attribution, distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize because it rewards an effector rather than a nuclease.
responses.response: The distinction from 2020 is fair: the effector chemistry is genuinely new, and the adenine deaminase that had to be evolved against an unnatural substrate is substantial chemistry. I withdraw some of my earlier suggestion that this is protein engineering around a known reaction. What I cannot resolve is the attribution. He himself lists the Nishida and Kondo cytidine-deaminase work as concurrent, so a single-laureate citation rests on a priority judgment the committee has not actually made. I rank B061 as my second alternative, and it would move above B007 for me if that priority question were settled in Liu's favour and safety data held up.

responses.point: Somfai pairs Buchwald and Hartwig on Pd-catalysed C-N coupling with Liu on base editing, and himself flags the overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize and Kosugi's precursor.
responses.response: I still regard C-N coupling as the second most mature and best-attributed option on the list, and I would not object to it. The clean two-person credit is a real advantage over my own ballot. But he is right that Kosugi and the 2010 prize weigh on it, and these are the same issues of precedent that I must apply to Barrer, Breck and Flanigen for B013. I would keep the question of novelty relative to earlier prizes consistent across the whole list.

uncertainties: Whether a sharp three-name B013 citation can be defended against Yu and Tsapatsis, and against the earlier framework-discovery work of Barrer, Breck and Flanigen.
Whether the committee will decide that a first approved degrader is needed before B007, and which of Ciulli, Handa and Sakamoto belongs in the third place.
How to resolve the Nishida and Kondo priority question for B061, and how much weight the 2020 CRISPR prize should carry.
My industrial-impact statements for zeolite catalysts rest on general knowledge and are not verified from the supplied files.
statement.conflict_note: No personal or institutional tie to Corma, Davis, Zones, Yu or Tsapatsis is stated in my profile. My research on structure determination of zeolites and porous frameworks by electron diffraction is scientifically close to B013, and Peter Brzezinski has noted that as a Stockholm University colleague he knows me. I disclose the proximity and have no recusal request; the committee may weigh my B013 judgment accordingly. I have no conflicts with B007, B061, B022, B001, B034, B068, B044, B032 or B049.
